items.title: Ukraine's attack on Saint Petersburg 'brings war back to Russia'
items.description: Volodymyr Zelensky called Kyiv's attack on Saint Petersburg a 'fair' response to the deadly Russian strikes on several Ukrainian cities a day earlier. It is also a testimony to Ukraine's growing capacity to strike further inside Russia. FRANCE 24's Douglas Herbert tells us what that means for Russia.

items.title: Iran strikes Kuwait's main airport, killing one passenger, as fragile ceasefire is tested again
items.description: In the first deadly strike on the Gulf since an April 8 ceasefire came into place, 63 people were also injured.

items.title: Israel’s invasion of southern Lebanon devastates centuries of history
items.description: From Phoenician temples to Crusader castles, heritage sites bear the brunt of Israel's expanding military offensive.

items.title: Democracy in Africa: Coups, crises and foregone conclusions
items.description: As Ethiopia formally counts the votes following Monday's election, attitudes toward democracy appear to be shifting across Africa. In April, Burkina Faso's junta leader told the Burkinabe people to "forget" democracy.

items.title: Iran and the US trade strikes in the Persian Gulf, further testing the ceasefire
items.description: Kuwait briefly shut the country's main airport after Iranian drones heavily damaged it and killed one person, the latest in a series of attacks by Iran and the U.S. that have tested a fragile truce.

items.title: Putin remains uncompromising on Ukraine, but is public discourse on war changing in Russia?
items.description: Russia is intensifying attacks in Ukraine but more than four years of war are causing concern even among Putin loyalists.

items.title: Iran war soured Gulf Arabs on Iraq. Can new leader in Baghdad win them back?
items.description: Iraq was offering attractive opportunities for Gulf Arab economic and diplomatic initiatives, but the war made it a springboard for Iran-backed militia attacks. Can the country’s young and untested prime minister navigate a multifaceted crisis?

items.title: Ukraine Bolsters Defenses Along Belarus Border Amid Concerns Of New Invasion
items.description: In Ukraine's Chernihiv region, along a section of the Dnieper River that divides Ukraine and Belarus, border guards are on the lookout for signs of another invasion from the north. In May, Kyiv warned that Russia was once again trying to draw Belarus into the war against Ukraine. Current Time correspondent Andriy Kuzak…

items.title: How This Russian Nuclear Waste Dump Became an Unlikely Victim of the Ukraine War
items.description: Europe poured millions into cleaning up a hazardous nuclear waste site in Russia's Arctic. The invasion of Ukraine brought the effort to a halt.

items.title: UN urges world not to forget Rohingya refugees as aid cuts threaten vital support
items.description: As the world approaches nine years since the mass displacement of Rohingya refugees from Myanmar into Bangladesh, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has appealed to the international community not to abandon the 1.2 million refugees living in the country, most of them in camps in Cox’s Bazar.

items.description: Zelensky told CBS News that Russia has been losing battlefield initiative since late 2025, creating a potential “window for negotiations” before winter.
